section_summary: This section traces State Department planning for Japan’s surrender and occupation, especially industrial disarmament, economic controls, democratic reform, reparations, labor, and civilian relief. It also contains Ikuo Oyama’s views on postwar Japan, debate over occupation committees and agrarian reform, correspondence on food supplies and Pacific island resources, and a draft relief policy that continues beyond page 260.

subfiles.title: Economic sections of post-defeat policy statement
subfiles.about: Transmits draft economic policy sections for Secretary’s Staff Committee review.
subfiles.summary: Martin explains the draft’s interagency review and its relation to CC-45 and longer-term policy.

subfiles.title: Summary of U.S. Economic Policy in the Initial Post-Defeat Period Relating to Japan
subfiles.about: Sets out proposed immediate occupation economic policies.
subfiles.summary: The draft covers industrial disarmament, economic control, reparations and restitution, democratic economic organizations, and restrictions on foreign credit.

subfiles.title: Economic Policy toward Japan
subfiles.about: Forwards Martin’s memorandum and draft economic section.
subfiles.summary: Notes differences from an earlier draft prepared with Mrs. Gulick.

subfiles.title: Economic sections of post-defeat policy statement
subfiles.about: Transmits occupation economic policy sections for review.
subfiles.summary: Martin describes interagency drafting and urges separate approval of longer-term principles.

subfiles.title: Summary of U.S. Economic Policy in the Initial Post-Defeat Period Relating to Japan
subfiles.about: States proposed initial occupation economic policies.
subfiles.summary: Repeats provisions on disarmament, economic control, reparations, democratic forces, and foreign credit.

subfiles.title: Japanese Post-War Problems
subfiles.about: Records Ikuo Oyama’s views on postwar Japanese politics and society.
subfiles.summary: Oyama favors democratic reform, civilian industry, free speech, and eventual Japanese-led change to the emperor institution. He opposes militarism and imperialism and discusses his possible return to Japan.

subfiles.title: Ikuo Oyama
subfiles.about: Traces Oyama’s education, academic career, and labor-party activism.
subfiles.summary: The sketch follows Oyama from Waseda and overseas study through anti-militarist activism, the 1923 Waseda dispute, leadership of workers’ and peasants’ parties, and his 1930 election to the Diet.

subfiles.title: Proposed broader committee on Japan
subfiles.about: Advises against creating a broader economic committee for Japan.
subfiles.summary: Grew proposes inviting Treasury and FEA representatives when their interests arise.

subfiles.title: Treasury proposal for a Far Eastern committee
subfiles.about: Reports concern over expanding the SWNCC Far Eastern Subcommittee.
subfiles.summary: Dooman says broader membership could impair the subcommittee’s effectiveness.

subfiles.title: Request for draft on workers’ organizations in Japan
subfiles.about: Requests FEA drafting assistance on Japanese workers’ organizations.
subfiles.summary: Mason asks for sections two and three by June 20.

subfiles.title: Invitation to Poll of Experts
subfiles.about: Invites Grew to answer a poll on postwar political change in Japan.
subfiles.summary: The bureau proposes anonymized publication of expert responses.

subfiles.title: Questions on Postwar Political Changes in Japan
subfiles.about: Asks experts about occupation, recovery, democracy, and the emperor system.
subfiles.summary: The form also requests professional and personal background.

subfiles.title: Reply to Poll of Experts invitation
subfiles.about: Declines poll participation because of Grew’s official position.
subfiles.summary: Grew expresses interest in the poll’s eventual findings.

subfiles.title: FEA reply on workers’ organizations draft
subfiles.about: Accepts the request to draft parts of the workers’ organizations paper.
subfiles.summary: Fowler promises delivery to Martin by June 20.

subfiles.title: Economic policy statements for Japan’s occupation
subfiles.about: Forwards two draft economic policy statements.
subfiles.summary: Martin describes their committee and departmental review status.

subfiles.title: Japan: Economic Policies During Military Occupation
subfiles.from: Interdivisional Committee on Economic Policy Toward Japan
subfiles.about: Details proposed economic measures for a full military occupation.
subfiles.summary: The paper assumes Japanese civil administration under military supervision. It addresses demilitarization, inflation, banking and fiscal controls, foreign assets, civilian supplies, labor rights, cartels, and relief, restitution, and reparations shipments. Its final section is cut off in the supplied text.

subfiles.title: General Provisions
subfiles.about: States broad U.S. objectives and initial military authority in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Calls for defeat, territorial changes, security, and eventual peaceful participation.

subfiles.title: Economic
subfiles.about: States occupation directives for Japanese economic activity.
subfiles.summary: Covers industrial disarmament, economic controls, reparations, democratic organizations, and foreign assets and credit.

subfiles.title: Treatment of Japanese Workers’ Organizations
subfiles.about: Outlines a proposed paper on Japanese labor organizations.
subfiles.summary: Calls for labor history, policy analysis, and recommendations.

subfiles.title: Note on attachment
subfiles.about: Refers to an attached document and possible remarks before a meeting.
subfiles.summary: Handwriting is too indistinct to establish further detail.

subfiles.title: Comments on June 23 Committee Minutes
subfiles.about: Requests corrections to minutes on economic policy toward Japan.
subfiles.summary: Hadley challenges qualifications placed on democratic reform, the stated purpose of military government, and conclusions about farm tenancy and industrial reform.

subfiles.title: Minutes of Interdivisional Committee on Economic Policy Toward Japan
subfiles.from: Interdivisional Committee on Economic Policy Toward Japan
subfiles.about: Records discussion of agrarian, industrial, and labor reform during occupation.
subfiles.summary: Members weigh agricultural reform against food production and occupation staffing. The minutes advise limited immediate measures on credit, taxation, prices, and tenancy, and discuss applying similar principles to industrial and labor organizations.

subfiles.title: Submission of surrender policy paper
subfiles.about: Submits Ray’s views on Japan’s surrender and postwar policy.
subfiles.summary: Ray asks officials to consider his attached recommendations.

subfiles.title: A surrender policy for Japan
subfiles.about: Argues that clear surrender terms could shorten the war.
subfiles.summary: Ray advocates a limited occupation, leaving the emperor institution’s future to the Japanese, and support for a liberal capitalist economy. He argues that imposed political or social changes could strengthen resistance and cites writers on occupation, Japanese politics, and self-determination.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of Ray’s paper
subfiles.about: Acknowledges Ray’s surrender-policy paper.
subfiles.summary: Dickover says he will circulate it to relevant officers.

subfiles.title: Routing note
subfiles.about: Asks Mr. Long to handle the attached material.
subfiles.summary: The brief handwritten note includes a later July 24 notation.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of Oyama materials
subfiles.to: Military Intelligence Division; Office of Naval Intelligence; Federal Bureau of Investigation; Office of Strategic Services
subfiles.about: Distributes the Oyama conversation memorandum and biography.
subfiles.summary: Sends the two items for their possible value to intelligence offices.

subfiles.title: Memoranda for Captain Wallace S. Wharton
subfiles.about: Requests forwarding of Japanese postwar materials to Wharton.
subfiles.summary: Lists a conversation memorandum and a request for biographical data.

subfiles.title: Routing note on Kahn memorandum
subfiles.about: Forwards a memorandum after Kahn and Thorp spoke.
subfiles.summary: Hallam says Thorp asked her to send it to Dort.

subfiles.title: Immediate Food Supplies for Chinese Port Towns
subfiles.about: Proposes using Chinese funds to speed food shipments to port towns.
subfiles.summary: Kahn suggests Dr. Soong could fund procurement or reimburse FEA.

subfiles.title: Geological survey of Japanese mandated islands
subfiles.about: Supports a survey of Pacific islands’ geology and resources.
subfiles.summary: Thorp offers State Department assistance with the proposed survey.

subfiles.title: Revised paper on Policy with Respect to Relief (Japan)
subfiles.about: Forwards a revised Japanese relief-policy paper.
subfiles.summary: Kahn says changes to basic policy papers required redrafting.

subfiles.title: Policy with Respect to Relief (Japan)
subfiles.about: Analyzes the occupation commander’s authority to provide civilian relief and imports.
subfiles.summary: The paper reads approved directives as placing primary responsibility for welfare on Japanese authorities. It recommends imports only when occupation security or broader objectives require them and Japanese efforts prove insufficient. It proposes disease rates as one measure of need and begins assessing minimum dietary levels. The paper continues beyond page 260.
